nodes.text: Smith Group Admin is the multi-tenant back office behind a group of mattress and furniture retailers. One CodeIgniter 4 application serves several stores, each with its own orders, staff, delivery zones and website, and the same app exposes the REST API that every store's storefront calls.

Staff scan paper invoices and the system turns them into orders, then carries each order through payment, delivery scheduling and customer messaging. Sales reps, managers, delivery crews and warehouse workers each see only the screens their role needs.

items: CodeIgniter 4
PHP
MySQL
JavaScript
Docker
CodeIgniter 4 / PHP 8 - explicit routing, thin controllers
Service layer - business rules kept out of controllers
MySQL - migrations, soft deletes and entities
Three access layers - session login for staff, token auth for the API, per-store keys for public storefronts
Queued email - sent by a CLI worker, not inline
Twilio - SMS and WhatsApp to customers
PrintNode - fax and print to each store's machine
AI document reading - Gemini extracts order details from scanned invoices
Network scanners - a small per-store agent feeds scans in
Telegram - live alerts for new activity and inquiries
Orders from scans: scan an invoice, review the extracted draft, confirm the sale
Payments & status: record payments and move each order through a five-step tracker
Deliveries & routes: 14-day capacity by zone, daily stop lists and an approval step
Message Centre: automatic order texts plus a chat view for SMS and WhatsApp replies
Sales floor mode: a kiosk screen for reps to log sales and see their standing
Roles: admin, manager, sales, delivery and warehouse accounts, each locked to its own screens

nodes.text: I built it as one application with clear boundaries: controllers only orchestrate, services hold the business rules, and custom validators guard every form. Routes are listed explicitly so nothing is exposed by accident, and an activity log records who did what for every important change. Long-running work such as email, fax and scanning runs through queues and CLI workers so the screens stay fast.
Screenshots use demo data. Customer names, contact details, addresses, scanned documents, staff photos and financial totals are blurred.

peb.seoTitle: Personal Expense Budgeting - Angular & Firebase App | Gregory Peter Yanoc
peb.description: Personal Expense Budgeting app built with Angular and Firebase by Gregory Peter Yanoc - track spending with real-time sync.

nodes.text: A comprehensive personal finance management application built with Angular and Firebase. This modern web application helps users track their daily expenses, categorize spending, and gain insights into their financial habits through an intuitive and responsive interface.

The application features real-time data synchronization, user authentication, expense categorization with visual icons, search and filtering capabilities, and responsive design that works seamlessly across all devices.

It also includes an AI-powered receipt scanner and voice entry (Google Gemini with OpenRouter, Groq and NVIDIA fallbacks), "Pebby" — an AI spending co-pilot — a statistics dashboard with daily/weekly/monthly trends, swipe-to-delete lists, and a runtime light/dark theme.

images.alt: Watchy home screen with rotating hero banner and Trending row

nodes.text: A Netflix-style movie and TV streaming app built with React 19, TypeScript and Vite, then packaged as a native Android app with Capacitor. Watchy serves a polished, dark, cinematic browsing experience with a rotating hero banner, horizontally-scrolling category rows, rich title modals, and a full-screen player.

Catalogue metadata — trending titles, a Netflix-on-TMDB row, genre rows, multi-search and trailers — is pulled live from The Movie Database (TMDB) API. Playback is served through a registry of embed providers with one-tap failover, so when one source is down the viewer simply switches to another.

The app is gated by Supabase authentication and driven by Supabase remote config: a force-update gate for stale APK builds, a global maintenance switch, and per-account disabling — all of which propagate to live clients within about a minute, no redeploy required.

TypeScript - Fully type-safe codebase
Vite 8 - Fast build & HMR dev server
Capacitor 7 - Native Android wrapper (hardware back button, splash, status bar)
Hand-rolled CSS - Custom dark, cinematic UI with skeleton loaders

localStorage Store - Continue Watching with cross-tab sync

Category Rows: Trending, Netflix, Action, Comedy, Sci-Fi, Drama and Thriller

nodes.text: This project demonstrates modern React and native-hybrid development practices including:

items: Custom Hooks: Data fetching, auth, version and account status isolated into reusable hooks
Provider Abstraction: Each stream source owns its own URL builder behind a single registry interface
External Store Pattern: Continue Watching uses a pub/sub store with referentially-stable snapshots
Fail-Open Config: Network/config errors never lock users out — the app keeps the last known good state
Defense in Depth: no-referrer frames, origin checks on postMessage, and a redirect/pop-up guard
Native Integration: Android back button, mixed-content handling and splash/status-bar theming

nodes.text: The application is actively under development with regular updates and feature additions. The project showcases my expertise in building cross-platform streaming experiences with React, TypeScript and Capacitor, backed by Supabase for auth and live remote configuration.

nodes.text: Entity Duel is a browser-based, Magic-style trading card game built with React and Vite. Two duelists race to bring each other from 20 life to 0 by playing lands for mana, casting creatures, sorceries and instants, and trading blows across clearly defined turn phases.

It ships with three ways to play: a single-player mode against a rule-driven AI opponent, a local Hotseat mode for two players on one device, and real-time Online PvP powered by Supabase. Players choose from six pre-built decks, each with its own archetype and identity - from Emberwood aggro to Stonewall control.

nodes.text: Entity Duel showcases interactive front-end engineering: a deterministic rules engine drives every card interaction, global game state is managed with Zustand, and Supabase provides real-time synchronisation for online matches. The AI opponent evaluates the board each turn to make its plays, and the whole experience is delivered as a fast, responsive single-page app.
